items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: that's the post where Geronimo was captured by Captain White, in 1875, I think it was.

ctx.x: -- then they began breaking up the -- our outfit was being broken up, you know, for -- this was when the war was at its worst. They had this big Battle of the Bulge incident. Then the order came down that no-one in the Armed Forces could move unless you were on the way to someplace. Wherever you are, stop, because everything's going to be turned around. So that broke up our band. It broke up the regiment and everything.

So then I remember I said to myself I was going to keep my nose clean and I wasn't going to -- least of all I wasn't going to get hurt, and I wasn't thinking about getting killed in nobody's army. So then I said now what'll I do? So we used to have -- in Huachuca, we used to call it -- the old post was an old National Guard post, and that's the post where Geronimo was captured by Captain White, in 1875, I think it was. That sort of thing. So there was a movie house up there, and these people had been living…

So anyway, while we were there they broke it up, so I said now I'm going to have to do something. So this particular day I just got up -- they were doing different things. They were coming around and giving you different duties and so on.
